title: Plecture configuration language
description: Structural schema for Plecture configuration. The root schema describes a definition document: a TOML file whose top-level tables are definition blocks, task included — a task declaration's instruction is its `instructions` array, each element either inline text or the content of a sidecar Markdown file. The reserved root files and the plugin/catalog manifests have their own entry points too, so the full set of anchors is #definitions, #config, #catalogs, #lock, #plugin, and #catalog. This schema is authoritative for accepted structural shapes until the implementation lands a schema generator whose output is conformance-tested against it. It deliberately does not encode cross-definition or evaluation-context rules, which are Plecture semantic validation, nor expression correctness, which is CEL validation.

definitionDocument.description: A discovered TOML file in a trusted definition root. Every top-level table is a definition block whose table name is the definition id.

propertyNames.$comment: PLECTURE-CFG-ID-INVALID. Dots separate address segments and hyphens are excluded because a task id is also a workflow node id.

definition.$comment: PLECTURE-CFG-KIND-MISSING when kind is absent; PLECTURE-CFG-KIND-UNKNOWN when it is outside the vocabulary.
definition.description: A definition block in a TOML definition document. Every kind is declared the same way — a table named by the definition id, carrying kind.

staticReference.description: A dotted definition address: the relative form <id>, or the catalog-qualified form <catalog-alias>.<plugin-path>.<id>. Never a tagged value, because static topology stays statically discoverable.
staticReference.$comment: PLECTURE-CFG-REF-DYNAMIC when a tagged value appears here.

executableName.description: A plugin-owned executable. A bare name resolves against the containing plugin's own executables. User-authored config uses the catalog-qualified slash form <catalog-alias>/<plugin-path> or <catalog-alias>/<plugin-path>/<executable-name>. Executable lookup is a separate namespace from definition references and keeps the slash grammar, because it must split an arbitrary-depth plugin path from an executable name.

literalScalar.$comment: PLECTURE-CFG-VALUE-TAG-SURFACE: a surface accepting a literal only rejects any tagged value.

anyOf.$comment: PLECTURE-CFG-VALUE-TAG-SURFACE: a literal-data object cannot be a tagged value.

from.description: A projection path. Its leading segment is the root; which roots are available is surface-specific and checked by Plecture semantic validation.

default.description: The value used when the source is absent. Mutually exclusive with optional.

optional.description: Absence propagates: a missing source omits the key rather than supplying a sentinel. Mutually exclusive with default.

expr.description: One CEL expression, parsed and checked against the environment declared for this expression site.

terminal.description: A terminal capability, resolved through whichever task in the plan declares the interactive endpoint.

json.description: A boundary serializer, not a CEL function. Its operand is a value tree whose leaves are literals or tagged values.

taggedValue.description: The complete tagged-value vocabulary. An object under a dynamic-value field that matches none of these forms is a structural error.

dataValue.description: A value on a surface that consumes data only: a literal, a projection, a computation, or a JSON serialization. No capability tags.
dataValue.$comment: PLECTURE-CFG-VALUE-TAG-SURFACE when a capability tag appears here.

bindingValue.description: A value on an action-binding surface, which may additionally consume a Plecture capability.

bindTable.description: An action binding: the values and capabilities crossing the Plecture/action boundary. Each key becomes a shell variable name.

command.description: A literal OS command name or path, resolved through the process environment. Never dynamic.

stdin.description: A value written to the process's standard input instead of its argv, for data that must not be visible in the process table.

execAction.$comment: PLECTURE-CFG-ACTION-BIN-AND-COMMAND when both are set or neither is.

script.description: Literal shell source. Plecture and CEL interpolation do not occur inside it.

action.$comment: PLECTURE-CFG-ACTION-TYPE-UNKNOWN for an unknown type; PLECTURE-CFG-ACTION-VARIANT when a field of the other variant is present.

noopAction.description: An action that does nothing and exits zero: a deliberate non-observation, legal only under [health.alive].

aliveAction.$comment: PLECTURE-CFG-ACTION-TYPE-UNKNOWN for an unknown type; PLECTURE-CFG-ACTION-VARIANT when a field of the other variant is present. The only site admitting the noop variant alongside exec and shell.

schemaDocument.description: A JSON Schema document, inline in TOML. Plecture annotations such as mutable may extend it. Plecture tagged values may not appear in it.

allOf.$comment: PLECTURE-CFG-VALUE-TAG-SURFACE: a contract document declares types, not values.

innerTable.description: The nesting joint, read from the surface being configured: the inner task's input object and its environment additions.

terminalTable.description: The task owns an interactive endpoint. send_text and send_keys receive their operand as the action's first positional argument. attach, capture, and pid receive no operand; pid returns the endpoint's root process pid.

chainDefinition.description: A chain fires against instances of the task document that declared it.

effectDefinition.description: An effect is a lifecycle-managed provider: contracts, health, an optional interactive capability, and composition. Its outputs are production records — immutable facts from setup plus nested projections. No completion contract and no live re-evaluation live here; both belong to the task document.

terminal.description: The task owns an interactive endpoint. At most one task in a plan declares it.

effectDefinition.$comment: PLECTURE-CFG-FIELD-UNKNOWN: the effect grammar is closed, and the completion contract is not in it. PLECTURE-CFG-HEALTH-ALIVE-REQUIRED when setup is declared without [health.alive].

workspace_provider_inputs.description: Literal data only: a workspace provider's hooks run before any node output exists.

max_up_children.description: Caps how many sessions parented on a session this workflow produces may hold run state "up" (any run-scoped task produced) at once. `plect up` rejects a child that would exceed this rather than queueing it. Unset means no cap.

channelInputSpec.description: A channel's per-key parameter shorthand, deliberately not a full JSON Schema document: only a channel input's presence is checked before delivery.

timeout.description: A delivery deadline, bounding one attempt. It reads author-declared parameters only; event data is excluded, so a delivery's own deadline can never be chosen by the event being delivered.

command.$comment: PLECTURE-CFG-REF-DYNAMIC: a channel's command is never chosen by data.

queryItemSchema.$comment: PLECTURE-CFG-FIELD-REQUIRED, PLECTURE-CFG-FIELD-TYPE: a query item schema is an object schema whose only required property is the string resource identifier.

configFile.$comment: PLECTURE-CFG-FIELD-UNKNOWN, PLECTURE-CFG-FIELD-REQUIRED: a reserved root file's surface is closed, a definition table is not part of it, and the dialect declaration is not optional.
configFile.description: config.toml, a reserved root file. It is not a definition file.

schema_version.description: The dialect this user config tree is written in. It governs the whole tree — every definition document, split across any number of files, inherits it — and is orthogonal to plect_min_version, which is binary compatibility rather than language dialect.
schema_version.$comment: PLECTURE-CFG-SCHEMA-VERSION-OLDER, PLECTURE-CFG-SCHEMA-VERSION-NEWER: which dialects are accepted is the loader's three-way comparison, not a structural bound, so no range is asserted here.

max_up_children.description: Caps every concurrently-up session whose logical parent is the virtual root.
max_up_children.$comment: PLECTURE-CFG-FIELD-TYPE: virtual-root capacity is a positive integer.

catalogsFile.description: catalogs.toml, a reserved root file: the catalog aliases registered on this machine and the plugins enabled under each.

lockFile.description: plect.lock, a reserved root file: the resolved revisions and content hashes mounting is verified against.

pluginManifest.description: plugin.toml at a plugin's root: the package's identity, its executables, and the services the resident process supervises.

catalogManifest.description: catalog.toml at a catalog root: the plugins the catalog publishes. Explicit enumeration, not directory presence, is what publishes a plugin.

effectOutputsTable.description: An effect's public output wiring. Its roots are fixed when the layer is instantiated: an inner output, this layer's locals, or this layer's inputs. A live root belongs to a task document's completion predicate, so re-evaluation is not a task concern.

effectOutputValue.$comment: PLECTURE-CFG-FROM-ROOT: a task output projects inner.outputs.*, locals.*, or inputs.* only, and never a live root.

extendsOwnSchemaShape.$comment: PLECTURE-CFG-EXTENDS-SCHEMA-SHAPE when a key other than type or properties is present.

taskDefinition.$comment: PLECTURE-CFG-FIELD-UNKNOWN, PLECTURE-CFG-FIELD-REQUIRED, PLECTURE-CFG-KIND-MISSING, PLECTURE-CFG-EXTENDS-INHERITED-FIELD when both extends and resource_observer are set.
taskDefinition.description: A task declaration. It is an ordinary definition block, declared the same way every other kind is. Its instruction is the resolved texts of its `instructions` array, joined by a blank line in declaration order. A document is authored and referenced by its id; an instance is created from it by dynamic instantiation and identified by its resource and instance name. A declaration carrying `extends` is an extension: it specializes the base it names, inheriting the base's resource_observer rather than restating it.

extends.description: The base task this declaration specializes: an ordinary task reference, restrained to a closed set of additive operations (appended instructions, appended chains, appended done_when leaves, and new or default-completing schema keys). The base is untouched and remains independently referable.

resource_observer.description: The resource observer this task is written for. Named after the kind it references, the same way a workflow's workspace_provider field is. Declaring it is what lets every key a check or a chain input reads be resolved against that observer's published state at load time, and what lets instantiation reject an incompatible resource up front. An extension does not declare this: it inherits the base's.

instructions.description: The instruction, as an ordered sequence of segments joined by a blank line. Each segment is inline text or a sidecar file, so a task built by composing segments (a base instruction plus an extension) can append rather than concatenate strings.

state_schema.description: This task's own state: the keys a reviewer or another session writes into an instance. Plain JSON Schema, with no mutability annotation — state is mutable by definition. Any state-holding definition declares its state this way.

instructionElement.$comment: PLECTURE-CFG-TASK-INSTRUCTION-ELEMENT when other than exactly one of text and file is present; PLECTURE-CFG-FIELD-UNKNOWN for any other key.
instructionElement.description: One segment of a task's instructions array: inline text, or a sidecar Markdown file carrying the text, relative to the declaring file and resolved within the same trusted layer.

completionKeyPath.$comment: PLECTURE-CFG-FROM-ROOT: a completion key reads resource.state.* or self.state.*.

exprLeaf.description: A predicate computed over the roots this surface observes.
